agent_summary:
Configuration lane on juice.lab.test (OWASP Juice Shop 20.2.0 behind nginx/1.30.5), HTTP/port 80 only — HTTPS/443 refused. 121 read-only requests plus one approved PUT method-probe. Reachable surface: SPA served from / with a catch-all (unknown non-API paths -> 200 index.html, unknown /rest|/api -> 404); /ftp, /encryptionkeys, /support/logs and /.well-known/csaf all have serve-index directory listings; static bundles main.js/styles.css/polyfills.js; REST/API under /rest and /api; /api-docs Swagger UI; /metrics; security.txt (root and /.well-known); CSAF metadata.

Items 1-8 DONE (test performed, result recorded):
- CONF-01: HTTP-only, nginx version disclosed, no TLS on 443.
- CONF-02: verbose Express stack traces on 403/406/500 leaking absolute paths and framework version; unauthenticated /rest/admin/application-configuration and /metrics; wildcard CORS (ACAO:* on every response, incl. hostile Origin); no CSP/Referrer-Policy/HSTS globally; weak CSP (script-src 'unsafe-eval') only on /profile; /api-docs has its own CSP.
- CONF-03: /ftp enforces a .md/.pdf extension allowlist (.bak/.yml/.pyc/.gg -> 403); alternate suffixes at web root return the catch-all, no source disclosure — but .kdbx is NOT covered by the filter (see CONF-04).
- CONF-04: /ftp lists backups (package.json.bak, package-lock.json.bak, coupons_2013.md.bak) and incident-support.kdbx is directly downloadable; /encryptionkeys (jwt.pub downloadable) and /support/logs listed; .git/.svn/.DS_Store/.env/common config files NOT present; traversal blocked.
- CONF-05: unauthenticated admin/info endpoints application-configuration, application-version, /metrics, /api-docs; /api/Users and /api/SecurityAnswers require auth; /admin, /server-status, /nginx_status, /actuator, /console not present.
- CONF-06: OPTIONS advertises GET,HEAD,PUT,PATCH,POST,DELETE; approved PUT to a non-existent path returned 200 (catch-all accepts arbitrary methods rather than 405). TRACE/XST not testable with the available read-only method set.
- CONF-07: no Strict-Transport-Security on any response; 443 does not answer (plaintext HTTP only).
- CONF-08: no crossdomain.xml / clientaccesspolicy.xml (both return the catch-all).

Items 9-11 N/A: CONF-09 OS file permissions not observable over HTTP (web-exposed over-permissive access captured in CONF-04/05); CONF-10 single in-scope host, no subdomains/dangling aliases; CONF-11 no cloud storage buckets referenced anywhere, assets served locally.

Leads recorded for review/other lanes: unauthenticated config+metrics disclosure (medium); /ftp listing + downloadable KeePass .kdbx (high) and jwt.pub; authenticated /rest/user/authentication-details returning all users (medium); /api/Users/:id reads arbitrary users (medium); /rest/basket/:id horizontal access to multiple baskets confirmed via basket/1 vs basket/2 (medium) — the IDOR/access-control leads are for the authorization/info lanes to validate. Note also GET /rest/saveLoginIp performs a state change (records last-login IP) on a GET.

leads.title: [agent] Authenticated user can read all users' authentication details

detail.text: GET /rest/user/authentication-details/ as low-privilege test account conf1 returned HTTP 200 with a 14540-byte JSON body containing many users' records (38 distinct email addresses were redacted by the gateway before storage; full response is evidence x53). A single ordinary authenticated customer can enumerate the whole user base's auth details rather than only their own. Likely also exposes TOTP secrets per the data model. For the authz/info-disclosure lanes to validate.

leads.title: [agent] Basket accessible by numeric id for a different account (possible IDOR)

detail.text: GET /rest/basket/1 as test account conf1 returned HTTP 200 with a 1310-byte JSON basket (evidence x63). conf1 is a freshly-registered account; whether basket id 1 belongs to it or to another user needs confirmation by comparing against conf1's own basket id. Flagging for the authorization lane to verify horizontal access control on /rest/basket/:id.

leads.title: [agent] Confirmed horizontal access to multiple baskets via /rest/basket/:id

detail.text: As test account conf1, GET /rest/basket/1 returned a 1310-byte basket and GET /rest/basket/2 returned a different 557-byte basket (evidence x63, x102), both HTTP 200. A single customer session can read more than one basket id, indicating missing per-user authorization on /rest/basket/:id (Juice Shop "view another user's shopping basket" issue). For the authorization lane to confirm which ids are foreign.

leads.title: [agent] Customer can read arbitrary user records via /api/Users/:id

detail.text: GET /api/Users/1 as low-privilege test account conf1 returned HTTP 200 with a 301-byte user record (an email address was redacted; evidence x99). An ordinary customer can read other users' account records by incrementing the id, enabling user enumeration/PII disclosure. For the authorization lane to confirm scope (which fields are returned).

GET /ftp/incident-support.kdbx returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type application/octet-stream and Content-Length 3246 (the full file is stored as evidence exchange x39). The /ftp file server blocks .bak/.gg/other extensions with 403 "Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!" but serves the .kdbx KeePass database unauthenticated, exposing a credential vault file for offline cracking.

leads.title: [agent] Exposed /ftp directory listing with backup files and verbose stack traces

detail.text: GET /ftp returns a directory listing (serve-index) of backup and sensitive files: coupons_2013.md.bak, package.json.bak, package-lock.json.bak, incident-support.kdbx (KeePass database), announcement_encrypted.md, encrypt.pyc, suspicious_errors.yml. Non-whitelisted extensions return 403 but the 403 body leaks full server-side stack traces including absolute paths /juice-shop/build/routes/fileServer.js and node_modules internals, plus Express ^4.22.1.

items.na_reason: [agent] OS-level file/directory permissions are not observable over HTTP with read-only requests. The web-observable over-permissive access (world-readable /ftp, /encryptionkeys, /support/logs directory listings and downloadable kdbx/jwt.pub) is documented under WSTG-CONF-04/05.
[agent] Only a single in-scope host (juice.lab.test) answers; no subdomains or dangling CNAME/aliases to third-party services are in scope or observable, so subdomain takeover cannot be tested here.

[agent] No cloud storage (S3/GCS/Azure Blob) buckets or URLs are referenced in the unauthenticated application-configuration, security.txt, CSAF metadata or the client bundle (main.js); all assets, promo video and uploads are served locally from the host, so there is no cloud storage surface to test.
